about: A Few Moments Later is one of the time cards from SpongeBob SquarePants: a dark blue background covered in blue-green flower shapes, the kind of card that pops up between scenes to tell the audience how much time has passed. In memes it is used as a punchline frame dropped between a setup and a consequence, or swapped for an absurd time skip. The humor relies on the show's narrated sense of comic timing, so a plain caption on the card reads in a dramatic narrator's voice.
origin: The time cards come from the Nickelodeon cartoon SpongeBob SquarePants, which began in 1999. They are read aloud by the show's French-accented narrator, and lines like "A few moments later" and "One eternity later" became instantly recognizable.
usage:
There is one large centered box on the card. The default text is "a few moments later", which works as a transition in a longer meme or a group chat story. For a joke on its own, change the time span to something exaggerated or painfully exact: "one eternity later", "6 business days later", "3 loading screens later".

Keep it short and in lowercase or title case so it looks like the show's card. It is perfect for slow processes: shipping, software updates, waiting rooms, matchmaking queues and replies from a crush.
